fair_value_reason: NTM EPS at Sep 2027 is $14.83 (25% of 2027E $14.0 plus 75% of 2028E $15.1, standalone, no buybacks); at 19x that is $282. The 2027E FCF-yield cross-check is $282-290. With a ~50% chance the decision slips, the probability-weighted merger effect is about -0.5% (~-$1), against +0.3% to +1% in round 1. Agent_2's three methods are one multiple view (~$284), agent_3's $270 is a legitimate skeptic judgment, and agent_5's base-rate method reads ~$287 when smoothed. Reconciled ~$282, plus a ~2% dividend not in the price.
supervisor_summary: The round-2 forecasts have converged (mean P>=274 0.545, fair values $270-285), and none of the remaining disagreements moves the price distribution by more than a few dollars. The biggest open question, STB timing, tilts toward a slip: under NEPA the Board cannot decide before the EIS is done, and that review had not formally started by late September. That makes no decision by Sep 2027 roughly a coin flip, which leaves the overhang and paused buybacks in place but removes the binary event. The 17% NSC spread mostly reflects a rail-wide diesel selloff and a longer timeline, not collapsing approval odds. I tilt the mean ladder slightly up (P>=274 to 0.552), set fair value at ~$282 plus a ~2% dividend and keep the thesis break at $215. UNP is a fairly valued, roughly market-like compounder with a merger overhang.
key_drivers: Standalone EPS path: 2025 reported $11.98, 2026E ~$12.90, 2027E ~$14.0, 2028E ~$15.1, with buybacks paused until the deal resolves. NTM EPS at the horizon is ~$14.83, so 19x gives ~$282.

STB timing: under NEPA no final decision can issue before the EIS is done, and the EIS notice of intent was not out by late Sep 2026. I put about a 50% chance on no decision by Sep 30, 2027, which keeps the overhang and paused buybacks but avoids a binary event.

Merger outcomes for UNP are about +/-5% (acceptable approval or rejection after the $2.5B fee) and -8% to -12% only for accepted heavy conditions. UP walks on widespread trackage rights or line sales and reassesses above ~$750M of conditions.

Diesel: spot $5.20-5.30 against a ~$4.25 Q3 average gives a Q3 (and possibly Q4) surcharge-lag drag of ~$0.05-0.10 a quarter, offset by truck-to-rail volume (carloads +5% QTD). The 9-11% September rail selloff priced much of it.
Multiple: ~19.9x forward today. The history of UNP returns from 19-21x starting multiples is roughly flat to +5% a year, which caps re-rating upside.
